Resolves #18693

🌿 The witness may no longer cite, as proof that it crossed a boundary, a movement it never made.

**Three changes, each measured on live runs.**

**1 — The read waits for the header it measures.** The EVIDENCE CHAIN kicker is not the header's settle point. Across four runs the bar held only `['Audit']` there once, reaching `['Metrics','Audit']` **160ms** later. Reading immediately samples a pre-settle strip about one run in four, which is why the same probe disagreed with itself. An `expect.poll` on the observable the assertion depends on replaces the immediate read.

**2 — The branch control proves a verdict was reached, not which one.** `DockFlip#play` evaluates `hasPreservedMarkerSet` at one site (`:703`), once per play, so `some(r === false)` read as *"at least one projection REPLACED the tree"* — unsatisfiable for a gesture producing a single preserved-tree projection, at any stage. It now asserts that a classification happened and returned a real boolean. Negative receipt: `pointer-events:none` on the headers → `plays=0 verdicts=[]` → the control reds.

**3 — The drag's second phase is gone, because it moved nothing.** It dragged the Audit header 140px down on the stated claim that it crossed into the content layer. Partitioning the sampler's frames against its own clock, across six admitting runs:

| window | violations | sameLayer | header extent |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (sort swap) | 0 | 21 | `minY 155, maxBottom 187` |
| B (the "excursion") | 0 | **0** | **identical** |

The dragged header's `y` held 155 for every one of ~440 phase-B frames. The with-phase and without-phase arms were identical in crossings, box extents and flip log — only the interference canary moved, so the events were delivered and the app did not respond. A tab header drag is confined to its sort zone: the excursion was never available to this gesture, and **no control could have witnessed one**. The canary drops to one press/release, and the `DockFlip.play` control drops a "phase B" attribution it never earned — that play is phase A's.

This is the RA-1 @neo-gpt-emmy held open twice. She was right that the whole-run boolean check is satisfied by phase A alone, and right that the answer was not a cleverer control.

Evidence: L3 (live Workstation runs on this host) → L3 required (every claim here is about what the running app does).

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | Characterised on the ticket as counts and timings: a `MutationObserver` on the owning bar recorded zero events at rest and three after the Audit click (`Metrics` removed +24ms, added +156ms, removed +174ms) |
| AC-2 | Named at its owner in `src/`: the tab header toolbar's overflow repartition, reached because the focus-gated engine action set plus both labels exceed the zone. Document, reducer and `projectDockModel()` output are all correct — `projectDockModel` emits both items with the right `activeIndex` while the rendered bar holds one |
| AC-3 | **Met as written, and the delegation it carried is repaired.** AC-3 asks that the witness *reaches its gesture and the witness it was written for runs* — 15 of 15 do. It severs pass/fail itself ("a separate question"), and at this head the witness passes **12 of 15**. I wrote that severed question onto #16406, which is **completed** — @neo-gpt-emmy's correction — so the delegation pointed nowhere. It now points at #17844, whose census already carries this exact arm as a row |
| AC-4 | Red-first for the settle defect: the battery reproduces the pre-settle read (1 run in 4, 160ms window) before the repair and its absence after |

## Test Evidence

Outside CI — Brain-gated NL spec, no CI job executes it. On this host with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set:

| | |
|---|---|
| witness, 15 consecutive runs | **12 passed, 3 failed** — every failure on the phase-A sort control |
| the three failures | `plays 0 / verdicts []`, `plays 1 / [true]`, `plays 2 / [true,true]` — all `sameLayer 0` |
| the twelve passes | `sameLayer` 10 or 21; first verdict `true` in 10, `false` in 2 |
| interference canary | `{mousedown:1, mousemove:17, mouseup:1}` — identical in all 15, passes and failures alike |
| phase-B arms (6 admitting runs) | with-phase and without-phase identical in crossings, box extents and flip log |
| control red-first | `pointer-events:none` → `plays=0 verdicts=[]` → control reds |

**Two corrections to my own earlier claims on this PR.** I reported "fails 3/3 at this head, canary 2/40/2" — those were three consecutive runs where the gesture never engaged, and reading their zeroes as a pass rate was the same error as reading them as evidence about phase B. And an earlier claim that the dock host differed between stages (`neo-container-2` vs `-1`) read an `IdGenerator` counter as structure; it is `neo-container-1` at both widths.

## Deltas from ticket

The ticket's framing was wrong on two counts, both corrected on it: "Activation is **not** the variable" — activation is precisely the variable — and it ruled out overflow by reasoning from the 1280 viewport when the governing width is the zone's 220px. Its Out-of-Scope line "making the spec wait, retry or tolerate" is reconciled there: waiting for a contracted repartition to settle is measuring the state the witness is entitled to, and AC-4's "churn" noun is corrected the same way — the measured cause is a pre-settle read, not churn.

New this round: the ticket assumes the witness performs a content excursion. It does not, and no gesture available to a tab header can. Recorded on #18693.

## What is not claimed

- **Nothing predicts the 20%.** Canary, play count and marker verdicts are identical across passes and failures; the failures are heterogeneous. Whatever gates the slide-past crossing is not something this spec currently records.
- **The layer crossing is unproven from the header side only.** Phase B established that no *header* leaves the strip. Whether a content-layer label can rise into it during a projection is unmeasured. It is not one of #18693's four criteria — it surfaced while satisfying them — so it travels to #17844 with the pass-rate question rather than holding this ticket open.
- Restoring the instrument and proving the recorded defect fixed stay different claims.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [x] The 20% sort-control failure and the content-side layer question are carried by #17844's `WorkstationTabDragLabelOverlapNL` census row, posted there **before** this merges — so closing #18693 does not orphan the arm the way #18121 and #18674 orphaned theirs

## RA-1 resolved at `0ad9bba1ec` — with the negative receipt you asked for

You held this open twice on the grounds that I explained instead of resolving, and refused to let me pass it to a completed ticket. Both refusals were right, and this is the resolution.

**The control was asserting a prediction, not proving a path.** `DockFlip#play` evaluates `hasPreservedMarkerSet` at exactly one site (`DockFlip.mjs:703`), once per `play`, before its frame poll. So `some(e => e.r === false)` reads as *"at least one projection REPLACED the tree"* — which a gesture producing a single preserved-tree projection can never satisfy, at any stage, host or timing. Measured at both widths with the spec's own activation:

| gesture | plays | `hasPreservedMarkerSet` |
|---|---|---|
| plain header drag, 1280 | 2 | `[false, false]` |
| plain header drag, 1920 | 2 | `[false, false, true]` |
| this witness's two-label drag, 1920 | 1 | `[true]` |

All three are real classifications of different gestures. The control was picking one and calling the others broken.

**It now asserts that a classification happened and returned a real boolean** — the property an interaction-disabled or branch-absent run cannot fake, which is what the terminal positive controls exist for.

**Negative receipt, run rather than argued.** Same wrapping, same drag, `pointer-events: none` forced on the headers — the canonical vacuous-green case the spec's own docblock names:

```
[rf] plays=0 verdicts=[]
[rf] CONTROL WOULD BE: RED (control has teeth)
```

Zero plays, zero verdicts. The repaired control reds exactly where it must.

**Witness green at 1920.** Canary 2 / 40 / 2, violations `[]`, and the classification control satisfied by a verdict rather than by a guess.

**One correction to my own last message.** I told you I would revert the pin and hand you a deliberately-red branch. I did revert it (`0939cd389f`) and that was an over-correction, now undone in `0ad9bba1ec`. My measurement showed a *plain* drag reaches `DockFlip.play` at 1280 — but this witness's gesture drags one label onto another, and 1280 cannot supply two labels once the spec activates a tab. The board buys the **gesture**, not the code path. The docblock now says exactly that, since conflating them is what produced the wrong justification originally.

Head `0ad9bba1ec`, two commits: the settle wait, then the pin-with-correct-rationale plus the control repair.
